objective.why: Customers act on these dates and fields. Today we cannot tell which of them to trust.

objective.note: Targets are proposed, not agreed. Edit them in docs/design/status.json.
why_points: The date can be wrong while labelled verified: one stored deadline was a registration date, and 12 of 39 stored deadlines read 'verified' on call status alone, not on the date.
Everything else we collect (organiser, sponsorship, categories, overview, about 24 fields) arrives at varying quality, from different sources, and none of it has been measured.
There is no method yet that proves a field's quality, so improvements are judged by feel and we correct after the customer complains.
The weekend research fails about 73% of its Gemini calls, September cost $134, and weeks of building still need manual rescue.
objective.why_close: So the project is as much a way to prove quality, field by field and step by step, as it is a way to collect data.
ladder: Stated: a model or page says so
Supported: it appears on the cited page
Proven: page and purpose checked by code

quality.not_measured: Sponsorship, overview and categories have no measure at all for conferences, and nothing beyond the deadline is measured for awards. The non-deadline facts rest on a small spot-check (docs/design/field_spotchecks.json). Conferences and awards are deliberately not blended. The old six-component weighted index was retired on 2026-10-03: its parts are now Complete and Accurate, and freshness is shown as process health.
quality.split_method: COMPLETE % = expected fields that are filled (a pinned honest blank counts as filled) averaged with coverage of customer-tracked events. Edition facts (start date, city, country, main page) are always expected; the call fields (deadline, link, evidence) are excused while the event starts more than 90 days ahead and no call is open, because nothing is published yet. ACCURATE % = proven / (proven + contradicted) over facts we state (deadline vs its cited page, start year vs edition, pinned facts, customer-verified dates, spot checks); unproven is shown beside it and never counted wrong; a contradiction is never excused by the 90-day rule. Awards have no event start: their grace is a Closed award with no new cycle announced (no deadline or opening date ahead, no open call).

manual_verification.definition: Events a person had to verify on the event's own page, as a share of the events we track (Cybersecurity and Utility market lists, today's count). Counted from the pin ledger (ruled_on) and the operator edits log (entries where the operator verified or ruled on a named event). A month is shown from the first one with a record (2026-10); the current month is partial; the denominator is today's roster, so past months are an estimate. It should fall as the research gets more right.
